page: Microsoft Azure FX32-16ms_v2 is an x86_64 instance engineered for memory-intensive workloads that require sustained high clock frequencies. Virtualized via Microsoft Hyper-V, the system is driven by a dedicated Intel Xeon 8573C processor operating at 4.2 GHz. The allocation yields 8 physical cores supporting 16 vCPUs via hyperthreading, supplemented by 48 KB L1 data cache, 2 MB L2 cache, and a large 260 MB shared L3 cache. Memory provisioning is notably heavy at 672.0 GB total RAM, providing 42.0 GB of RAM per vCPU. Hardware capabilities include Intel Advanced Matrix Extensions (AMX tile and INT8) and AVX-512 vector instructions. No local storage is bundled with the instance, requiring external premium network storage for persistent disk access, and zero GPUs are included.

Benchmark results highlight the advantages of high clock speeds combined with a large cache hierarchy. Single-core evaluation reveals top-tier performance, achieving a Geekbench single-core score of 2336.0, as well as strong throughput in single-threaded gzip compression at 34.66 GB/sec and bzip3 decompression at 14.31 GB/sec. Uncached large-block memory write throughput reaches a strong 90.97 GB/sec, while cached small-block reads achieve 1380.46 GB/sec. Conversely, multi-threaded throughput remains in the middle tier of tested hardware, with Geekbench multi-core scoring 13705.0 and stress-ng multi-core registering 17762.82, bounded directly by the 16-thread hardware ceiling.

The primary tradeoff of the FX32-16ms_v2 lies in its asymmetric compute-to-memory distribution and the absence of integrated high-speed local scratch disks. Workloads demanding extreme thread parallelism will encounter compute bottlenecks despite the expansive memory pool. However, for applications with licensing models tied strictly to core counts, the configuration offers advantageous cost efficiency by concentrating 672.0 GB of system RAM across only 16 vCPUs. Primary operational fits include electronic design automation, memory-bound database engines, caching clusters, and single-threaded enterprise applications requiring massive working memory.
description: Microsoft Azure FX32-16ms_v2 is a memory-dense server designed for workloads that require high single-core execution speed alongside an exceptionally large memory capacity. Driven by an x86_64 Intel Xeon 8573C processor operating at 4.2 GHz, the machine supplies 16 dedicated vCPUs across 8 physical cores and 672.0 GB of system memory, establishing a 42.0 GB per vCPU ratio. Benchmark tests indicate top-tier single-core performance in Geekbench alongside strong single-threaded compression and uncached memory write throughput. The instance includes no bundled local storage and zero GPUs, relying on external network volumes for storage operations. While multi-core throughput is constrained by the 8-core count, the dense memory allocation makes this instance qualitatively cost-effective for core-licensed environments. It is well matched for in-memory databases, electronic design automation, large-footprint financial simulations, and analytical memory caches.
